Solve rates are the number of reported crimes cleared by arrest or by exceptional means divided by the number of reported crimes. A crime is [cleared by exceptional means](https://ucr.fbi.gov/crime-in-the-u.s/2019/crime-in-the-u.s.-2019/topic-pages/clearances){target='_parent'} when an agency cannot arrest or charge the person who committed it but has done all of the following:

a) Identified the person who committed the crime
b) Gathered enough evidence to support an arrest, make a charge, and turn the person over to the court for prosecution
c) Identified the suspect’s exact location so that the person could be taken into custody immediately
d) Encountered a circumstance outside the agency’s control that prevents it from arresting, charging, and prosecuting the person

Examples include the death of the person who committed the crime, a victim who refuses to cooperate with prosecution, and a denied extradition. Agencies can also clear cases reported in earlier years, so a year’s solve rate can exceed 100 percent.
